summary: This resolution changes House voting procedures for the 119th Congress by requiring the Clerk to announce pairs from a signed written list immediately before vote results, publish that list in the Congressional Record after non-voters, and limit announcements to once per legislative day.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a House procedural resolution governing the announcement of voting pairs during floor votes. It contains no provisions related to appropriations, expenditures, or government budgets.
The resolution addresses only internal House voting procedures for pairs and has no connection to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No text in the bill pertains to healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
The bill is silent on firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the resolution relates to immigration, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
The resolution has zero connection to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No text involves welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net spending.
The bill does not mention schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances appear in the text.
The resolution is unrelated to sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
Nothing in the bill addresses tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The measure contains no fiscal provisions that would affect deficits or the national debt.
The bill is silent on LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
No language concerns foreign assistance or international aid.

While the resolution governs a narrow aspect of House floor voting mechanics (announcement of pairs), it does not address public elections, voter access, voter ID, or election integrity measures. It is purely internal parliamentary procedure and therefore has no bearing on the topic as defined.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No text addresses worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The resolution does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
